comment: Playback regression manifest. Items live in the Jellyfin library built from ~/Movies/development-videos (flat TNN naming). mode: what useVideoPlayback must choose. validate: 'copy' = remuxed video is stream-copied so its packet hashes match the baseline exactly; 'devtc' = video re-encoded on device (VideoToolbox), tolerant checks only; 'subsync' = server-HLS lane, asserts mpegts segments and WebVTT timestamp-map alignment; 'none' = mode + progress assertions only. progressMin: seconds playback must reach; playSeconds: how long the driver lets the item play. Durations below 45s get lowered thresholds. playSeconds must leave real headroom before the file ends: validation probes the LIVE remux session, and reaching EOF tears it down so ffprobe gets a 404 (T26, a 27.1s file, played 24s and failed this way).

items.title: T05 REMUX H264 TrueHD
items.comment: Its one SUBRIP track is flagged forced AND default, which is the shape that lost the track entirely: shipped FORCED=YES it was withheld from AVKit's picker and never applied, so a file with cues at 2.253s showed nothing. The only fixture that pins the rule that a subtitle group must always advertise something the viewer can reach.

items.title: T06 SERVER H264 PGS burnin
items.comment: H.264 + TrueHD + one PGS track. Was transcode: the server re-encoded the whole file to paint the subtitles into the picture. The engine decodes them to bitmaps the app draws, so the video copies and the TrueHD is carried losslessly. Its four cues sit at 6.3s, 11.2s, 15.3s and 28.3s with PGS erase sets between them, which makes it the timing fixture.

items.title: T10 REMUX HEVC HDR10 PQ
items.skip: tvOS SIMULATOR rejects the PQ master (NSURLError -1002) and the server HDR transcode too; the PQ path was built against real-device behavior (-12927). Run with --only T10 on a device build to verify.

items.title: T31 DEVTC VP6 MP3
items.comment: Tiny file: the device transcode reaches EOF in seconds and the 20-segment rolling window evicts the head. The 2026-08-07 note here claimed the loopback server then 404s those segments forever, which is no longer true and may never have been: segmentURL queues a seek-restart for any out-of-window request (Remuxer.swift), pruneSegments never touches init.mp4, and the pipeline parks at EOF waiting for a seek rather than returning. Hash validation is probably liftable now; it needs a fixture that plays past keepWindow and seeks back, which the driver cannot yet express.

items.title: T32 DEVTC ProRes 422
items.comment: ProRes decodes to yuv422p10le, which h264_videotoolbox does not take. Refused outright before libswscale was vendored, so this was a server transcode of camera footage. Expects h264 because the source is 10-bit only in chroma sampling terms; the depth gate reads the container's declared format.

items.title: T33 DEVTC MJPEG 422
items.comment: Full-range 4:2:2 (yuvj422p). Old camera and screen-recorder output, and a second colour range through the scaler.

items.title: T34 DEVTC FFV1 lossless
items.comment: Lossless archival in 4:2:2. Compressed, unlike rawvideo, which is why it is worth pulling over a LAN and rawvideo is deliberately excluded from the codec list.

items.title: T35 DEVTC HuffYUV
items.comment: The other lossless one. Registered decoder, never reachable before the converter existed.

items.title: T36 DEVTC VP9 10bit
items.comment: The strongest assertion in this group: expects HEVC, not H.264. A 10-bit source opens hevc_videotoolbox with p010le instead of being declined as 'bit depth over 8-bit'. If this reads h264 the depth branch in VideoTranscoder.init did not fire.

items.title: T37 DEVTC MPEG2 interlaced
items.comment: field_order tt, the shape of a DVD rip. Asserts the deinterlace lane runs at all; combing is not machine-checkable.
items.skip: The deinterlace pass is a per-pixel Swift loop: 10.8 fps at -Onone against a 24fps source, 3333 fps at -O. The harness needs a Debug build because the probe is __DEV__-only, so the lane cannot keep up here. Release reaches 8.3s with 46s buffered. Routing the pass through avfilter (bwdif/yadif_videotoolbox, both enabled in the build) removes the cliff.

items.title: T38 DEVTC MPEG4 ADPCM
items.comment: MPEG-4 video the engine already transcoded, with ADPCM audio that used to send the whole file to the server anyway. The old-AVI shape exactly.

items.title: T39 REMUX mixed carriable audio
items.comment: One AC-3 track carried, one WavPack track dropped: WavPack has no decoder in the linked build. audioRenditions=1 is the assertion, because before the per-track change this whole file went to the server over that one track.

items.title: T90 DEVTC MPEG2 TS subsync
items.comment: MPEG-2 in TS with a container start_time of 2.82s, a burned-in clock, and a sidecar .srt with cues at 5s, 15s and 30s. Covers a shape nothing else did: non-zero start_time through the engine with text subtitles. It does NOT settle the open anchor question. Remuxer fixes sessionAnchorUs to the first keyframe, so output time is source time minus 2.82s, but Jellyfin serves SIDECAR cues in 0-based file time, which tracks the picture either way. Exposing the anchor needs an EMBEDDED text track, which Jellyfin extracts at source PTS. The clock makes any drift visible by eye meanwhile: the cue reading FIVE SECONDS must appear as the burned-in clock passes 00:00:05.

items.title: T92 DEVTC AV1
items.comment: AV1 without hardware decode: libdav1d decodes in software, VideoToolbox re-encodes. Our dav1d is built under a private symbol prefix so it cannot collide with the copy expo-image links for AVIF.

items.title: T41 SERVER VP9 10bit gate-reject
items.comment: VP9 4:2:0 10-bit at 1920x804, under the pixel gate. The title still says SERVER and gate-reject because it must match the file on disk, which is how the driver resolves the item; the expectation is what changed. It used to be declined as 'bit depth over 8-bit' because h264_videotoolbox is 8-bit only and there was no converter. There is now: hevc_videotoolbox takes p010le, so this encodes as HEVC. Expecting hevc rather than h264 is the assertion - if it reads h264 the depth branch in VideoTranscoder.init did not fire.

items.title: T42 SERVER DivX3 no-decoder
items.comment:
TITLE IS A JOIN KEY, not a description: the harness resolves fixtures by Jellyfin item name / file stem, so it must keep matching 'T42 SERVER DivX3 no-decoder.avi' on disk even though the name is now wrong. Renaming it broke resolution for the whole run once already.

The lane it tests has inverted. DivX 3 was never missing from FFmpeg; MPVKit's --disable-decoders allowlist switched it off. We build FFmpeg ourselves now, so this file plays on the engine and no longer reaches the server. Kept because it is real content where T93 is synthetic.

items.title: T43 SERVER H264 PGS short
items.comment: The case that proves the routing change. H.264 720x480 with one PGS track and no audio at all: it direct-plays on codec alone, so once burn-in stopped forcing the server it would have played with no subtitles whatsoever. Image subtitles are now themselves a reason to reach the engine. Also the only fixture whose PGS canvas (1280x720) differs from its video, so it is what exercises the scale and letterbox maths.

items.title: T44 SERVER Theora SRT subsync
items.comment:
Guards the server-HLS subtitle-sync invariant (2026-08-10 Star Trek bug). Theora has no decoder in the app's FFmpeg build, so this file deterministically takes the server lane with its embedded SRT riding as a WebVTT rendition; the driver asserts mpegts segments and |X-TIMESTAMP-MAP - segment PTS| <= 0.5s. Video carries a burned-in clock and the cues echo it, so any offset is also visible by eye on a device.

BROKEN TRIGGER, needs a fixture regeneration. This file reached the server because its video codec had no decoder in the build. It has one now, so the engine takes it and the subtitle-sync invariant this guards is no longer exercised. The replacement trigger must be codec-independent: encode above TRANSCODE_MAX_PIXELS (2,100,000 px) the way T40 does, which forces the server lane no matter what decoders exist. Until then treat a pass here as unproven.
items.expectedFailure: server-lane trigger no longer fires; see comment

items.title: T45 SERVER DivX3 SDH subsync
items.comment:
Same invariant as T44 but on real content: a 90s dialogue clip from a broadcast episode, video re-encoded to DivX3 (msmpeg4v3 has no registered decoder in the app's FFmpeg, so the engine always declines) carrying the episode's real English SDH track. T44 proves the timing mechanically; this one lets a human judge cue timing against actual speech.

BROKEN TRIGGER, needs a fixture regeneration. This file reached the server because its video codec had no decoder in the build. It has one now, so the engine takes it and the subtitle-sync invariant this guards is no longer exercised. The replacement trigger must be codec-independent: encode above TRANSCODE_MAX_PIXELS (2,100,000 px) the way T40 does, which forces the server lane no matter what decoders exist. Until then treat a pass here as unproven.
items.expectedFailure: server-lane trigger no longer fires; see comment

items.title: T54 DIRECT audio OGG
items.comment: Vorbis in Ogg: AVPlayer decodes neither the codec nor the container, so this used to direct-play, fail on the device and retry on the SERVER, re-encoding a music file to reach a device that could have rewrapped it. Audio-only items reach the engine now (video-less session, Remuxer.runPipeline hasVideo), so the mode is localRemux and the retry is gone. This line flipping is the signal that audio-only support landed. The title still says DIRECT because it has to match the file on disk, which is how the harness resolves the item in Jellyfin; renaming the file would re-id it.

items.title: T55 DIRECT audio OGA
items.comment: Same shape as T54, in the .oga extension Jellyfin also serves as Ogg.

items.title: T56 REMUX audio WMA
items.comment: Audio AVPlayer cannot open, reaching the engine through the video-less session that used to be a hard 'no video stream' failure. Was TTA, which does not work: the build has the TTA decoder but NOT the TTA demuxer, so the file cannot be opened at all. Checking the decoder list without the demuxer list is how that slipped through. WMA satisfies all three - Jellyfin's ffmpeg encodes it, the asf demuxer is enabled, wma* decodes - and it is re-encoded to FLAC on the way out.

items.title: T60 REMUX AC3 5.1
items.comment: T60-T88 are the surround and lossless set, built by `npm run make:test-media`. Each `expect` was written as a PREDICTION from the rules in AudioTranscoder (AAC and ALAC copy, FLAC copies when its extradata is a 34-byte STREAMINFO, everything else decodes to FLAC at the source's own channel count) and then tested; the baselines were only recorded once every prediction held. audioChannels and audioBitDepth guard the two silent degradations, a downmix and a 24-to-16-bit truncation, neither of which changes the codec name. audioCopy on T62/T65/T66 compares packet payloads against the source file, which is the only thing that separates a copy from a lossless re-encode. Verified to have teeth: asserting it on re-encoded T63 fails.

items.title: T62 REMUX FLAC 7.1 24bit
items.comment: Eight channels. Today maxChannels=6 downmixes it to 5.1; it is also the case that breaks ALAC, whose only 8-channel layout is 7.1(wide).

items.title: T66 REMUX ALAC 5.1 24bit
items.comment: The one lossless source that already survives: ALAC is in the copy set, so this guards against a regression rather than describing a defect.

items.title: T80 REMUX EAC3 7.1 real
items.comment: Real E-AC-3 7.1. FFmpeg's eac3 encoder tops out at 5.1, so this case cannot be synthesised and has to be a downloaded sample.

items.title: T82 REMUX AC3 5.1 real
items.comment: The runt of the T80-T88 group at 30s where the rest run 78s to 120s, which is presumably why it was trimmed to 12s of play for EOF headroom. That was over-cautious and made it the only item in the suite with no slack: it was the sole failure of a 55-item run under load, reaching 2s of the 8s it needed, then passed at exactly 8/8 when re-run alone. 14s matches its neighbours and still leaves 16s before EOF, against the 3s that actually broke T26.

items.title: T83 REMUX EAC3 channelcheck
items.comment: Dolby's own channel-identification clip: each channel announces itself, so a mapping or downmix error is audible by ear on a device where host-side validation cannot reach.

items.title: T89 REMUX EAC3 channelcheck resume
items.comment: Same file as T83, opened from a server-side resume point so the app auto-seeks on load and the engine takes its seek-restart path. Every Continue Watching launch does this, and the suite covered none of it: resetResume cleared the position before every item, so the restart path only ever ran on a real device. Validation still probes the LIVE session afterwards, so a restart that leaves the stream unservable fails here instead of on a TV.

items.title: T84 REMUX EAC3 matroska
items.comment: Six seconds long, so hash validation cannot run: the stream reaches EOF inside the 30s window the driver hashes and the rolling segment window evicts the head, the same tiny-file limitation recorded on T31. The expect assertions above still run (they need no baseline), and T61/T81/T83 cover E-AC-3 passthrough with hashes.

items.title: T85 REMUX TrueHD real
items.comment: A real Blu-ray extract: VC-1, TrueHD plus four AC-3 tracks, and 13 PGS subtitle tracks. All 13 carry no language and no title, which is why it is the fixture for subtitle track identity: Jellyfin labels every one of them the same, and the app used to key the viewer's pick on that label, collapsing all 13 onto the last one. It expected `transcode` for months because getBurnInSubtitleStream returns a track whenever every subtitle stream is image-based, which made canRemuxLocally decline and handed the server the whole file to re-encode. In-app image subtitles removed that decline and this line flipping to localRemux is the signal it worked. Note the video is VC-1, so it now goes through the on-device VideoToolbox encoder rather than the server's; the audio is what is carried untouched.

items.title: T86 REMUX DTS-HD MA real
items.comment: Same shape as T85 with H.264 video, DTS-HD MA and seven audio tracks, plus four PGS tracks, all four untagged. Flips to localRemux for the same reason, and here the video copies outright. Also the worst case for concurrent renditions: the pipeline builds one per audio track and produces them all in the same pass, now with four subtitle decoders alongside.

items.title: T87 REMUX DTS 5.1 real
items.comment: DTS-ES, seven channels. Today's min(channels, 6) downmixes it; it is the item that proves the channel cap moved.

items.title: T88 REMUX EAC3 JOC Atmos real
items.comment: Genuine Dolby Atmos (E-AC-3 with JOC), lifted from Apple's own HLS example stream and copied in byte for byte. ffprobe reports 'Dolby Digital Plus + Dolby Atmos'. Passthrough has landed: the expect block above asserts ec-3, the Atmos profile and a packet-level copy, and it passes. The receiver displaying DOLBY ATMOS was confirmed on device 2026-08-12.

items.title: T93 DEVTC DivX3
items.comment: DivX 3 (msmpeg4v3). Went to the server not because FFmpeg lacks the decoder but because MPVKit's prebuilt build switched it off with --disable-decoders. We build FFmpeg ourselves now and every native decoder is enabled. ffprobe reports msmpeg4v3 while the decoder is called msmpeg4, which is why the allowlist carries the ffprobe name.

items.title: T94 DEVTC DV NTSC 411
items.comment: The fixture that proves the libswscale path. DV NTSC decodes to yuv411p, and the hand-written 8-bit packer it replaced assumed 4:2:2 chroma, so it read three quarters of every chroma row out of alignment padding. It never failed, it returned a plausible picture with wrong colour, which is why nothing caught it. 720x480 at 29.97 because DV is format-locked.

items.title: T95 DEVTC Cinepak
items.comment: Cinepak, the fourth codec the old allowlist switched off. Also the only fixture whose decoder outputs rgb24 rather than a planar YUV format, so it exercises a conversion the hand-written path had no branch for at all. 320x240 because the Cinepak encoder runs at ~0.3x realtime.

items.title: T96 DEVTC Theora real
items.comment: Theora, the fourth codec MPVKit's --disable-decoders allowlist switched off, and the only one of the four we cannot generate: no Theora ENCODER exists in either ffmpeg on this machine. Real sample from samples.ffmpeg.org, video stream copied untouched into Matroska. Shorter window than the other coverage fixtures because the source is ~10.5s. Carries no audio, so it doubles as the video-only session path.
